annotations.title: Prepare interview questions from a resume

description: Builds a job interview prep set for a project, program or product manager, TPM, PMO lead or business analyst from their resume text and, if they have it, the job posting. Use it when someone shares a resume (pasted or attached) before an interview, or asks what a hiring manager will ask them. Returns: the resume lines a hiring manager is likely to press on, each with a question that quotes the line and the points a strong answer covers; each requirement of the posting covered, partial or a gap, with the gaps as questions; and behavioral questions for the role. Each question has an id to pass to check_interview_answer when the person practises it. Optional: company (adds questions from what some large US employers publish, with source links), interview_date (adds the days left and what to practise first). Fixed rules written by practitioners, the same result for the same text. English text; contact details are removed first; nothing is stored.

bullets.description: The bullets of this role, each copied word for word.
bullets.title: Bullets

company.description: Employer, as written in the resume.
company.title: Company

dates.description: Dates of the role, as written, for example Jan 2019 - Present.
dates.title: Dates

title.description: Job title, as written in the resume.
title.title: Title

certifications.description: One credential per item, word for word.
certifications.title: Certifications

skills.description: Skills or tools lines, word for word.
skills.title: Skills

company.description: Optional. The employer's name as written in the posting.
company.title: Company

industry.description: Optional. The employer's industry, one of healthcare-life-sciences, financial-services, software-saas, government-public-sector, consulting-services, retail-supply-chain, manufacturing-industrial, energy-utilities; a plain name such as healthcare or banking is also read. Adds questions written for that industry. Empty when not sure.
industry.title: Industry

interview_date.description: Optional. The interview date as YYYY-MM-DD.
interview_date.title: Interview Date

job_posting.description: The full text of the job posting, as the person gave it. Optional; with it the result adds the requirements, the gaps and questions about them.
job_posting.title: Job Posting

job_requirements.description: Optional. The requirement lines of the job posting, each word for word from job_posting; lines that are not are left out and counted in the result. Without them the requirements are read from job_posting.
job_requirements.title: Job Requirements

lang.description: The language the person writes in, as a code such as es, fr or ru; empty or en for English. The result names this language; findings are written in English.
lang.title: Lang

resume_outline.description: Optional structure of the resume: roles with title, company, dates and bullets; summary; skills; certifications; education. Every line must appear word for word in resume_text; lines that do not are left out and counted in the result. Without it the plain text is read.

resume_text.description: The resume as plain text, copied in full from what the person pasted or from the text of the file they attached. At least the summary and the experience section.
resume_text.title: Resume Text

role.description: Optional. One of project-manager, program-manager, technical-program-manager, product-manager, scrum-master, pmo, it-manager, business-analyst, delivery-manager; a title as written (for example Senior Program Manager) is also read. Empty when not sure.
role.title: Role
